To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) students who reported they would not cheat for punitive reasons reported higher levels of cheating and less responsibility for academic integrity, and (2) students who reported that they would not cheat due to reasons related to learning, character, and/or morality reported less cheating and greater responsibility for academic integrity.

(1) students who said they would avoid cheating because of punitive consequences, such as getting caught and punished, were more likely to have cheated in classes; (2) students who said that they would avoid cheating for reasons related to the importance of learning, personal integrity, and/or because it is simply wrong were less likely to have cheated; and (3) students who took responsibility for promoting academic honesty were more likely to avoid cheating and to have less of a tendency to cheat.
